key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move and how the surrounding fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. Its physics-informed approach connects individual particle paths with the broader flow field.
problem_solved: Reconstructing fluid flow and predicting long-range particle trajectories when only sparse measurements of particle motion are available.
method: Combines a Lagrangian view of moving particles with an Eulerian view of flow at fixed spatial locations.
Uses physics-informed learning to jointly predict particle trajectories and flow fields from limited trajectory data.
Validates the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: The work illustrates how physical constraints can support learning from sparse observations. It offers a promising approach for practitioners building models that must capture both local motion and system-wide fluid dynamics.
visual_elements: Sparse measured trajectory segments extending into predicted long-range particle paths.
A side-by-side diagram contrasting particle-following Lagrangian and fixed-location Eulerian views.
A pipeline showing trajectory measurements entering TrajectoryFlowNet and producing paths plus a flow-field map.
Paired simulation and blood-vessel illustrations highlighting the two validation settings.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
